resources.heading: Where can I get help?
resources.subtitle: Trusted organizations to help you settle in Canada.
resources.emptyText: We're carefully selecting trusted organizations for you. Check back soon.
resources.noPartnersInCategory: No active partners in this category yet.
resources.notFound: This resource is no longer available.

gettingSettled.label: Getting Settled
gettingSettled.description: Settlement agencies and programs to help you find your footing.

findWork.label: Find Work
findWork.description: Job boards, mentorship, and career support for newcomers.

immigrationHelp.label: Immigration Help
immigrationHelp.description: Licensed consultants for permits, PR, and citizenship.

librariesLearning.label: Libraries & Learning
librariesLearning.description: Free programs, spaces, and resources at your local library.

communityBelonging.label: Community & Belonging
communityBelonging.description: Local nonprofits and community centres open to everyone.

networksPlanning.label: Network & Planning
networksPlanning.description: These organizations coordinate services across BC. They work with agencies rather than serving individuals directly.

internationalStudents.label: International Students
internationalStudents.description: Campus services for study-permit holders, who most settlement programs cannot serve.

insurance.label: Insurance
insurance.description: Travel, visitor, and health coverage for you and visiting family.

money.label: Money & Banking
money.description: Bank accounts, credit, and financial guidance for newcomers.

diversecity.tagline: Culturally safe programs across education, employment & wellbeing.
diversecity.description: DIVERSEcity Community Resources Society is a BC-registered charity (since 1978) that connects newcomers to culturally safe programs across education, employment, health, and wellbeing — the on-the-ground service arm for immigrant and refugee support in Greater Vancouver.
diversecity.eligibility: Settlement services are open to permanent residents, refugees and protected persons through IRCC funding. Temporary residents, international students, naturalized citizens and refugee claimants are served through the BC Newcomer Services Program.
diversecity.howToStart: For settlement services, email newcomers@dcrs.ca or call 604-507-6060. General enquiries: 604-597-0205.

settlement-services.name: Settlement Services
settlement-services.description: One-on-one work with a settlement worker to build a plan covering education, employment, housing and health.
settlement-services.eligibility: Permanent residents, refugees and protected persons through IRCC funding; temporary residents, international students, naturalized citizens and refugee claimants through the BC Newcomer Services Program.

linc.name: English Classes (LINC)
linc.description: Free English classes for new immigrants, from pre-literacy to CLB 4. A language assessment comes first.

safe-haven.name: Safe Haven Program
safe-haven.description: Settlement, employment, language and counselling support for refugee claimants who cannot use federally funded services.
safe-haven.eligibility: Refugee claimants in Surrey and Delta who are not eligible for federally funded settlement services.

rise.name: RISE Program
rise.description: One-on-one help and group workshops for refugees, covering community connection, Canadian systems, housing and employment.

employment-programs.name: Employment Programs
employment-programs.description: Job readiness and self-employment support, including EVolve Skills, Future Leaders, H.E.A.L. for Work and the Diverse Entrepreneurs Business Incubator.

early-childhood-education.name: Childminding During LINC
early-childhood-education.description: Free care for children 18 months to five years while a parent attends English classes.

mental-health-and-substance-use-services.name: Mental Health and Substance Use Services

language-testing-centre-celpip.name: Language Testing Centre (CELPIP)
language-testing-centre-celpip.description: CELPIP language testing for immigration and citizenship applications.

burnaby-neighbourhood-house.tagline: Community programs, childcare, and newcomer support in Burnaby.
burnaby-neighbourhood-house.description: Burnaby Neighbourhood House helps people enhance their lives and strengthen their community through programs built around the changing needs of a diverse population — childcare, family and food security, and dedicated newcomer support.
burnaby-neighbourhood-house.eligibility: Settlement services are funded by IRCC and, in line with its requirements, focus on permanent residents and convention refugees. Community, food and childcare programs are open to everyone.
burnaby-neighbourhood-house.howToStart: Call or email the nearest house. For settlement services, contact settlementprogram@burnabynh.ca or 604-431-0400.
burnaby-neighbourhood-house.hours: South House Mon–Fri 9:00am–5:00pm · North House Mon–Fri 9:30am–4:30pm · Brentwood House Mon–Fri 9:00am–4:00pm

newcomers-settlement-services.name: Newcomers Settlement Services
newcomers-settlement-services.description: Settlement plans, benefit applications, language support and community connections.
newcomers-settlement-services.eligibility: Funded by IRCC and, in accordance with their requirements, focused on supporting permanent residents and convention refugees.

information-and-orientation.name: Information and Orientation
information-and-orientation.description: Plain-language information for newcomers, one-on-one, as a family, or in a group workshop.

naars.name: Needs and Asset Assessment (NAARS)
naars.description: Wrap-around settlement support in your first language and in English, including help applying for benefits.

community-connections.name: Community Connections
community-connections.description: Volunteering, youth and women’s programs, English conversation circles, and workshops on health, work and education.

food-security.name: Food Security Programs
food-security.description: Food access programs, alongside Burnaby Meals on Wheels.

child-care.name: Child Care Programs
child-care.description: Licensed care for ages 0–12: early years, preschool, school age, afterschool and summer day camp.

volunteer-income-tax-program.name: Volunteer Income Tax Program
volunteer-income-tax-program.description: Free help filing your income tax return.

ymca-bc.tagline: Programs for families, children, and seniors across BC.
ymca-bc.description: YMCA BC supports families, children, and seniors in communities across British Columbia, building vibrant and healthy communities with a shared sense of social responsibility where people can thrive in spirit, mind, and body.
ymca-bc.howToStart: Email the newcomer team at newcomers@ymcabc.ca to enrol before your first session. General employment enquiries go to employment.services@ymcabc.ca, or call 604-681-9622.

english-conversation-club.name: English Conversation Club for Newcomers
english-conversation-club.description: A weekly club at the Robert Lee YMCA in downtown Vancouver where newcomers practise English with trained facilitators.
english-conversation-club.eligibility: All immigration statuses except visitor visas. You must be legally able to work in Canada. Temporary foreign workers should ask the team about separate sessions.

citizenship-test-prep.name: Prepare for the Canadian Citizenship Test
citizenship-test-prep.description: A hybrid group program that works through the Discover Canada guide with a facilitator and practice questions. Four sessions a year.
citizenship-test-prep.eligibility: All immigration statuses except visitor visas.

connect2work.name: Connect2Work for Newcomers
connect2work.description: Workshops that bridge settlement and employment: job skills, confidence, and connections in the local job market.

international-students-employment-suppor.name: International Students Employment Support
international-students-employment-suppor.description: Free program to help international students overcome employment barriers in Canada.

self-employment-program.name: Self Employment Program
self-employment-program.description: A 48-week funded program: 10 weeks writing a business plan, then 38 weeks of launch support with a case manager.
self-employment-program.eligibility: 18 or older; eligible to work in Canada; unemployed or working under 20 hours a week; applied for or received EI in the last five years, or receiving PWD/PPMB benefits; living in the Lower Mainland, Squamish or Sechelt; and you need a specific business idea.

explore-child-care-career.name: Explore Child Care as a Career
explore-child-care-career.description: A short course for newcomers on child care careers, the credentials needed, and how to get into the field.

wellness-connection.name: Wellness Connection for Newcomers
wellness-connection.description: A supportive space that welcomes newcomers and promotes good health.

iec-bc.tagline: Helping BC employers hire and retain immigrant talent.
iec-bc.description: The Immigrant Employment Council of BC works on the employer side of immigrant integration — helping BC businesses recruit, hire, and retain skilled immigrant talent through mentorship programs, job boards, and employer education.
iec-bc.howToStart: Register online through the TalentConnect form, or contact the office by phone or email. Each program has its own registration form.

talentconnect.name: TalentConnect
talentconnect.description: A free profile that shows BC employers your skills, education and experience, plus access to job postings and networking events.
talentconnect.eligibility: Newcomers with a work permit (except temporary foreign workers), and people approved for immigration who have not yet landed. You must be available for work and living in BC, or willing to move there.

mentorconnect.name: MentorConnect
mentorconnect.description: Occupation-specific mentoring that pairs you with an established local professional for up to 12 hours over two months.
mentorconnect.eligibility: Newcomers to Canada within the past 10 years who are eligible to work and have a job-ready resume. You must be in BC or planning to move to BC.

ascend.name: ASCEND
ascend.description: Online, self-paced learning to build the workplace soft skills Canadian employers look for (English & French).

fast.name: FAST
fast.description: Helps newcomers see how their experience and training meet Canadian standards, with career-prep streams by field.
fast.eligibility: Permanent residents or people approved in principle for PR, refugees, international students, skilled immigrants with a valid work permit, and Canadian citizens.

newcomer-jobs-canada.tagline: A job board built for newcomers to Canada.
newcomer-jobs-canada.description: Newcomer Jobs Canada is a commercial national job board that matches new Canadians with employers. It is a listings site rather than a settlement agency: there is no BC office and no in-person service. Employers pay to post; creating a job-seeker account is free.
highlights: Easier job search for new arrivals
newcomer-jobs-canada.howToStart: Create a free account online, upload your resume and apply for jobs on the website.

canada-shaw-immigration.tagline: Licensed RCICs, Canadian immigration & visa service experts.
canada-shaw-immigration.description:
Established in 2015 and based in Richmond, British Columbia, Canada Shaws Consulting Inc. is a member of Shaws Global Brand Group. Its immigration consultants are licensed by the College of Immigration and Citizenship Consultants (CICC), Canada’s regulatory body for immigration and citizenship consultants.

Canada Shaws provides comprehensive support across a wide range of Canadian immigration programs, as well as study permits, work permits, and business and investment pathways. Together with its sister companies under Shaws Global Brand Group, it also offers business consulting, investment advisory, global immigration services, residency and citizenship planning, education planning, and career planning. The firm helps clients worldwide navigate their options and build personalized plans for their future, with services available in English, Filipino (Tagalog), Persian (Farsi), Mandarin, and Cantonese.
canada-shaw-immigration.howToStart: Book a free introductory session to discuss your needs and learn about their services.

study-in-canada.name: Study in Canada
study-in-canada.description: Explore educational opportunities in Canada with personalized guidance on school applications, study permits, and — where eligible — part-time work during your studies and potential pathways to permanent residency after graduation.

work-in-canada.name: Work in Canada
work-in-canada.description: Navigate Canadian work permit options with professional support tailored to your career goals.

permanent-residency.name: Canadian Permanent Residency
permanent-residency.description: Explore permanent residency pathways tailored to your qualifications, experience, and long-term goals in Canada.

visas-extensions.name: Visas & Extensions
visas-extensions.description: Get assistance with visa applications, permit extensions, and maintaining your temporary resident status in Canada.

other-services.name: Other Services
other-services.description: Access support with citizenship applications, document amendments, Permanent Resident Travel Documents (PRTDs), Access to Information and Privacy (ATIP) requests, and other services.

global-connect-immigration.tagline: Registered consultancy for PR, visas, and settlement.
global-connect-immigration.description: Global Connect is a registered Canadian immigration consulting firm helping newcomers navigate permanent residency pathways, visa processes, and settlement planning with expert, personalized guidance.
global-connect-immigration.howToStart: Phone, email, or book a consultation through the website.

family-sponsorship.name: Family Sponsorship
family-sponsorship.description: Help sponsoring a spouse, partner, children or parents for permanent residency.

burnaby-public-library.tagline: Inclusive spaces to gather, learn, and play.
burnaby-public-library.description: Burnaby Public Library creates inclusive spaces where people can gather, learn, and play across four branches — free programs, resources, and places to connect.
burnaby-public-library.eligibility: Membership is free for anyone who lives in Burnaby or the surrounding InterLINK area. No identification is required to open an account, and you can use the name of your choice. Special memberships cover people living elsewhere in BC and outside BC.
burnaby-public-library.howToStart: Walk in to the service desk at any of the four locations, or call 604-436-5400, and staff will open your account and give you a card you can use straight away.

become-a-member.name: Become a Member
become-a-member.description: Staff open your account at any service desk and give you a card the same day. No identification needed, and an existing card from another library can be linked.
become-a-member.eligibility: Free for anyone who lives in Burnaby or the surrounding InterLINK area.

english-conversation-circle.name: English Conversation Circle
english-conversation-circle.description: Practise English and meet people in a relaxed group. A librarian leads the discussion. Runs in branches and on Zoom.
english-conversation-circle.eligibility: Ages 18 and over. Some English is recommended.

learning-english.name: Learning English
learning-english.description: Books, CDs and DVDs at every level, study guides for IELTS, TOEIC, TOEFL and CELPIP, and free online courses including Mango Languages and Road to IELTS.

arrivals-in-english.name: Arrivals in English
arrivals-in-english.description: A free online course built around the everyday English newcomers need while settling into life in Canada.

services-for-immigrants-newcomers.name: Services for Immigrants & Newcomers
services-for-immigrants-newcomers.description: A staff-maintained directory of Burnaby-area services by need — citizenship preparation, work, English — with each organization’s contact details and eligibility.

summer-reading-club.name: Summer Reading Club
summer-reading-club.description: Free summer reading program for children of all ages.

surrey-libraries.description: Surrey Libraries connects people, sparks curiosity, and inspires lifelong learning to enhance the lives of Surrey residents across ten branches.
surrey-libraries.eligibility: You can become a member if you live in Surrey or a neighbouring InterLINK community. Newcomer library services are free at every branch.
surrey-libraries.howToStart: Visit the Newcomer Welcome Centre at City Centre Branch, Level 4 — 604-590-7847 or library-newcomers@surrey.ca.

newcomer-welcome-centre.name: Newcomer Welcome Centre
newcomer-welcome-centre.description: A dedicated space on Level 4 of City Centre. Staff help with library cards, City of Surrey and community services, English questions and job searching. Holds world-language books, dictionaries, IELTS material and computers.

free-settlement-services-for-newcomers.name: Free Settlement Services for Newcomers
free-settlement-services-for-newcomers.description: Settlement workers from Options, DIVERSEcity, PICS and S.U.C.C.E.S.S. hold sessions in branches — job searching, English classes, citizenship exam prep, benefits, school registration.
free-settlement-services-for-newcomers.eligibility: No status restriction is stated. Services are delivered by partner agencies — call ahead to confirm times and locations.

english-language-learners.name: English Language Learners Programs
english-language-learners.description: Book clubs and conversation circles where you practise English in a friendly group. Sessions run across the branches.

newcomer-teen-social-club.name: Newcomer Teen Social Club
newcomer-teen-social-club.description: A monthly club where newcomer teens make friends and practise speaking English around a different topic each month.

get-a-library-card.name: Get a Library Card
get-a-library-card.description: Free for anyone living in Surrey or a neighbouring InterLINK community. Bring ID showing your name, photo and address, or two pieces of ID. Surrey residents can start online with a 90-day digital card.
get-a-library-card.eligibility: You can become a member if you live in Surrey or a neighbouring InterLINK community.

books-in-world-languages.name: Books in World Languages
books-in-world-languages.description: Collections in languages other than English, with a list of which languages each branch holds.

technology-help.name: Technology Help
technology-help.description: Drop-in and one-on-one sessions on computers, the internet, phones, tablets and eReaders.

vancouver-public-library.tagline: Free places to discover, create, and share.
vancouver-public-library.description: Vancouver Public Library has served the lifelong learning, reading, and information needs of Vancouver residents for over 100 years across 21 branches — free places for everyone to discover, create, and share ideas and information.
vancouver-public-library.eligibility: A free library card is for anyone who lives in or owns property in the City of Vancouver, and for residents of the University Endowment Lands, UBC neighbourhoods and UBC family housing. Programs and events are open to everyone.
vancouver-public-library.howToStart: Walk in to any branch with identification to register for a card, or register online for a temporary digital card. You can also call 604-331-3603 or email info@vpl.ca.

get-a-library-card.name: Get a Library Card
get-a-library-card.description: Register at any branch with ID, or online for a temporary digital card. A PR card, Confirmation of Permanent Residence, or a visa or work permit issued for six months or more is accepted, with proof of a Vancouver address.
get-a-library-card.eligibility: Free for people who live in or own property in the City of Vancouver.

esl-conversation-practice.name: ESL Conversation Practice
esl-conversation-practice.description: Conversation circles where English learners meet, practise and make friends. Most sessions are drop-in with no registration.
esl-conversation-practice.eligibility: Best suited to intermediate English speakers.

immigration-and-settlement-guide.name: Immigration and Settlement Guide
immigration-and-settlement-guide.description: A staff-maintained guide covering immigrating to Canada, settlement services, refugee support, finding work, learning English and translation services.

translation-services-guide.name: Translation Services Guide
translation-services-guide.description: A list of translation and interpretation services, including DIVERSEcity, ISSofBC, MOSAIC and the Society of Translators and Interpreters of BC.

clarity-english.name: Clarity English
clarity-english.description: A free online language-learning resource with interactive activities, practice tests and grammar help.

world-languages-collection.name: World Languages Collection
world-languages-collection.description: Reading for adults, teens and children in sixteen languages other than English. Branch collections follow their neighbourhoods; Central carries the full range.

big-brothers-big-sisters.description: Big Brothers Big Sisters matches children and teens with caring adult mentors. In this region the local agency is Big Brothers of Greater Vancouver, which runs the community, in-school and group mentoring programs listed here. Other parts of Canada are served by their own local agencies.
big-brothers-big-sisters.howToStart: In Greater Vancouver, apply through Big Brothers of Greater Vancouver: application form, guardian information session, family interview and pre-match training, then a waitpool for matching. Elsewhere, use the "Find an agency near you" locator on the national website.

community-mentoring.name: Big Brothers Community Mentoring
community-mentoring.description: One-to-one mentoring in your own community. Mentors commit to a weekly 2–4 hour outing for a year.

in-school-mentoring.name: In-School Mentoring
in-school-mentoring.description: One-to-one mentoring during the school day — a mentor visits for an hour a week through the school year.

teen-mentoring.name: Teen Mentoring
teen-mentoring.description: Secondary students mentor elementary students for an hour a week after school, with a youth leadership component.

mentoring-with-math.name: Mentoring with Math
mentoring-with-math.description: Tutoring plus mentorship to build confidence in maths, for families who cannot afford paid tutoring. Supplies are included.

game-on.name: Game On!
game-on.description: A group program on healthy choices through physical activity and life-skills discussion. 90 minutes a week for 8–10 weeks.

roots-mentoring.name: Roots Mentoring
roots-mentoring.description: Mentoring that celebrates Indigenous cultures, with learning from Indigenous community leaders.

united-way-bc.tagline: Support for the people who need it most across BC.
united-way-bc.description: United Way BC serves over five million British Columbians, delivering resources and support where they're needed most — emergency response, children & youth, seniors, poverty, mental health, and food security.
united-way-bc.howToStart: For help finding a service, call or text 2-1-1 — free and confidential. For questions about United Way BC itself, call 604-294-8929 or email info@uwbc.ca.

211.name: 211 British Columbia
211.description: Dial or text 2-1-1 for free, confidential referral to community, government and social services. Interpretation in over 240 languages and dialects.

bc-safe-haven-program.name: BC Safe Haven Program
bc-safe-haven-program.description: Supports refugee claimants through volunteer mobilisations and public appeals for housing and services.

food-security.name: Food Security
food-security.description: Programs that improve access to healthy food for people facing food insecurity across BC.

transit-assistance.name: Emergency Transit Assistance Program
transit-assistance.description: Transit vouchers so people in need can travel by bus at no cost.

better-at-home.name: Better at Home
better-at-home.description: Non-medical help for seniors — groceries, housekeeping and social connection — in 260+ communities.

school-s-out.name: School's Out
school-s-out.description: Before- and after-school programs with nutritious meals and developmental support during the school year.

work-experience-opportunities-grant.name: Work Experience Opportunities Grant
work-experience-opportunities-grant.eligibility: People receiving income assistance or disability assistance.

trout-lake-community-centre.tagline: 200+ programs for people of all ages.
trout-lake-community-centre.description: Trout Lake Community Centre offers more than 200 programs for people of all ages — a welcoming neighbourhood hub in East Vancouver run in partnership with the Vancouver Park Board.
trout-lake-community-centre.howToStart: Drop in and ask at the front desk, call 604-257-6955, or register online through the City of Vancouver recreation system.

leisure-access-program-lap.name: Leisure Access Program (LAP)
leisure-access-program-lap.description: City of Vancouver subsidy giving up to 50% off program and fitness centre fees.
leisure-access-program-lap.eligibility: Low-income Vancouver residents holding a valid leisure access card.

tlcca-program-cost-assistance.name: TLCCA Program Cost Assistance
tlcca-program-cost-assistance.description: Help with program fees for community members in financial need.
tlcca-program-cost-assistance.eligibility: Community members in financial need who are not eligible for LAP.

adaptive-programs.name: Adaptive Programs
adaptive-programs.description: Inclusive activities for all ages and abilities.

licensed-preschool.name: Licensed Preschool
licensed-preschool.description: Early learning for young children at the community centre.

older-adult-programs.name: Older Adult Programs
older-adult-programs.description: Stay active and connected with peers.

amssa.tagline: The backbone supporting BC's newcomer-serving agencies.
amssa.description: The Affiliation of Multicultural Societies and Service Agencies of BC is a provincial umbrella organization that strengthens the settlement and diversity sector — providing training, resources, e-learning, and advocacy for the agencies serving newcomers across BC.
amssa.eligibility: AMSSA serves member agencies and settlement-sector organizations, not individual newcomers. If you need help yourself, contact an AMSSA member agency directly.
amssa.howToStart: Organizations can call 604-718-2780 or 1-888-355-5560, email amssa@amssa.org, or apply through the membership page. Individual newcomers should contact an AMSSA member agency directly.

re-settlement-and-integration.name: (Re)Settlement and Integration
re-settlement-and-integration.description: Capacity building, networking, training and information resources for settlement service providers in BC and Yukon.
re-settlement-and-integration.eligibility: Settlement-sector organizations and professionals, including IRCC BC and Yukon and BC Settlement program holders.

migrant-worker-hub.name: Migrant Worker Hub
migrant-worker-hub.description: Tools, resources, service mapping and training that build the capacity of organizations supporting migrant workers in BC.
migrant-worker-hub.eligibility: Settlement and migrant worker support organizations.

amssa-institute.name: AMSSA Institute
amssa-institute.description: An online learning platform — webinars, AMSSATalks, lectures and e-learning on topics from refugee mental health to employment standards.

canadian-humanitarian-assistance-respons.name: Canadian Humanitarian Assistance Response (CHAR)
canadian-humanitarian-assistance-respons.description: A community-based network that distributes donations and essential supports to newcomers in need across Canada.

indigenous-truth-and-decolonization.name: Indigenous Truth and Decolonization
indigenous-truth-and-decolonization.description: AMSSA’s programme of Indigenous truth and decolonization work within the settlement sector.

national-sector-engagement.name: National Sector Engagement
national-sector-engagement.description: Coordinates national engagement initiatives and governance structures across the settlement sector.

surrey-lip.tagline: 30+ organizations coordinating newcomer integration in Surrey.
surrey-lip.description: An IRCC-funded, multi-stakeholder council that brings together 30+ community organizations to develop collaborative, research-driven strategies for newcomer integration in Surrey. Managed by DIVERSEcity, it also offers tools like a services map and a racism-reporting tool.
surrey-lip.eligibility: Surrey LIP is a partnership of organizations and does not deliver services to individuals. If you need help yourself, use the Surrey Services Map or contact a Community Connector.
surrey-lip.howToStart: For one-to-one settlement help, contact a Community Connector: CCBD@dcrs.ca or 604-547-1272 (Black diaspora), CCM@dcrs.ca or 604-547-1131 (Muslim and Afghan communities). To find any service in Surrey, use the Surrey Services Map. Organizations can use the contact form on the website.

community-connector-project.name: Community Connector Project
community-connector-project.description: Trained community members give newcomers information, services and connections during settlement, with streams for the Black diaspora and for Muslim and Afghan communities.
community-connector-project.eligibility: Newcomers of all backgrounds, with a particular focus on Black and Muslim/Afghan communities in Surrey.

surrey-services-map.name: Surrey Services Map
surrey-services-map.description: An online map of the services available to newcomers and residents in Surrey.

immigrant-advisory-round-table.name: Immigrant Advisory Round Table
immigrant-advisory-round-table.description: A table of immigrant residents that feeds community input into Surrey LIP’s planning and projects.

youth-newcomer-council.name: Surrey Youth Newcomer Council
youth-newcomer-council.description: A council of newcomer youth that brings youth perspectives into Surrey LIP’s work.

bridging-indigenous-and-newcomer.name: Bridging Indigenous and Newcomer Communities
bridging-indigenous-and-newcomer.description: A project that builds relationships and shared understanding between Indigenous and newcomer communities in Surrey.

first-peoples-guide.name: Surrey First Peoples Guide
first-peoples-guide.description: A guide that helps facilitators introduce newcomers to the First Peoples of the Surrey area.

delta-lip.description: The Delta Local Immigration Partnership is an IRCC-funded partnership table bringing local organizations together to make Delta more welcoming for newcomers. It states that it does not provide direct services to individuals.
highlights: Coordinates local newcomer services in Delta
delta-lip.eligibility: Delta LIP is a partnership of community organizations, agencies, municipal bodies and local businesses, and does not deliver services to individuals. Newcomers and youth can take part through its advisory tables, or find services through the Delta Services Map.
delta-lip.howToStart: Email deltalip@dcrs.ca, or use the contact form on the website. To find a service in Delta, use the Delta Services Map.

delta-services-map.name: Delta Services Map
delta-services-map.description: An online map of services available to newcomers in Delta.

resource-library.name: Resource Library
resource-library.description: Settlement and community resources published by the partnership for Delta residents and service providers.

delta-youth-newcomer-advisory-table-dyna.name: Delta Youth Newcomer Advisory Table (DYNAT)
delta-youth-newcomer-advisory-table-dyna.description: Brings together young people who want to make Delta more welcoming for newcomer youth.
delta-youth-newcomer-advisory-table-dyna.eligibility: Youth aged 16 to 25 who want to make Delta a more welcoming and inclusive place for newcomer youth.

immigrant-advisory-table.name: Immigrant Advisory Table
immigrant-advisory-table.description: A volunteer roundtable with members representing a diversity of backgrounds and experiences.
immigrant-advisory-table.eligibility: Applicants must be at least 26 years old.

sfu-international.tagline: Advising, orientation, and newcomer support for SFU students.
sfu-international.description: Simon Fraser University's International Services for Students supports international students with non-academic advising, orientation, and career programming, plus dedicated support for students who identify as refugees or newcomers.
sfu-international.eligibility: International students enrolled at SFU, including undergraduate, graduate and exchange students.
sfu-international.howToStart: Drop in (in person or virtual), book an advising appointment, or email iss_office@sfu.ca. Advising enquiries go to intl_advising@sfu.ca.

international-and-newcomer-student-advis.name: International and Newcomer Student Advising
international-and-newcomer-student-advis.description: Non-academic advising for international undergraduate, graduate and exchange students.
international-and-newcomer-student-advis.eligibility: International students, including undergraduate, graduate and exchange students.

refugee-and-newcomer-programs.name: Refugee and Newcomer Programs
refugee-and-newcomer-programs.description: Case-managed support for students who identify as refugees or newcomers — settlement help, orientation, and connections to academic advising, health, financial aid and career services.
refugee-and-newcomer-programs.eligibility: SFU students who identify as refugees or newcomers.

student-refugee-program.name: Student Refugee Program (with WUSC)
student-refugee-program.description: SFU sponsors six undergraduate refugee students from overseas camps each year with World University Service of Canada. The sponsorship covers tuition, books, fees and living costs.
student-refugee-program.eligibility: Refugee students aged 18–25 in overseas refugee camps, selected through WUSC.

global-student-centre.name: Global Student Centre
global-student-centre.description: A campus space at AQ 2013 for international student support, events and time with advisors.

international-student-orientation-series.name: International Student Orientation Series
international-student-orientation-series.description: A multi-part series for all new international students beginning studies at SFU.
international-student-orientation-series.eligibility: New international students starting at SFU.

international-student-career-week.name: International Student Career Week
international-student-career-week.description: A week-long series of career activities designed for international students.

fraser-international-college.tagline: Pathway college programs leading into SFU degrees.
fraser-international-college.description: Fraser International College is a private pathway college on SFU's Burnaby campus, offering foundation and first-year programs that lead into Simon Fraser University degrees. All programs are tuition-based.
highlights: Located on the SFU Burnaby campus
fraser-international-college.eligibility: Applicants must be at least 17 years old by the last day of their first semester and submit all academic transcripts. Academic requirements vary by program and by country of origin.
fraser-international-college.howToStart: Apply online through the FIC student portal, email info@fraseric.ca, or apply through a listed education agent.

foundation-program-utp-stage-i.name: Foundation Program (UTP Stage I)
foundation-program-utp-stage-i.description: Pre-university program taken over two terms.
foundation-program-utp-stage-i.eligibility: Successful completion of Year 11 or equivalent, with benchmarks depending on the chosen program.

international-year-one-utp-stage-ii.name: International Year One (UTP Stage II)
international-year-one-utp-stage-ii.description: First-year university credit programme leading into an SFU degree.
international-year-one-utp-stage-ii.eligibility: Generally Year 12 completion or equivalent; requirements vary by country system and program.

associate-of-arts-degree.name: Associate of Arts Degree
associate-of-arts-degree.description: Two-year associate degree taken at FIC.

student-success-team.name: Student Success Team
student-success-team.description: Academic advising and study planning, including graduation and transfer planning into SFU.

wellness-office.name: Wellness Office
wellness-office.description: Counselling and mental health support from a counsellor on staff.

student-support-services.name: Student Support Services
student-support-services.description: Attendance support, tutorials and workshops, document requests, accommodation help, orientation and campus events. FIC students also reach some SFU services, including SFU Recreation and SFU Multifaith.

tugo.tagline: Travel and visitor insurance, including cover during the health-plan wait.
tugo.description: TuGo is a Canadian-owned travel insurance provider with its head office in Richmond, BC. Its Visitors to Canada plans cover emergency medical costs for family visiting from abroad and for people waiting for a provincial health plan to take effect.
highlights: Emergency medical cover for visitors to Canada
Canadian-owned, head office in Richmond, BC
tugo.howToStart: Start a quote online through a TuGo insurance partner, or call 1-855-929-8846.
tugo.hours: Mon–Fri 6:00am–5:00pm PST · Sat 7:00am–4:00pm PST · Sun closed

visitors-to-canada-insurance.name: Visitors to Canada Insurance
visitors-to-canada-insurance.description: Emergency medical protection for visitors — doctor’s fees, prescriptions and emergency transport — with options covering pre-existing conditions.
visitors-to-canada-insurance.eligibility: For people visiting family or friends, travelling in Canada, or waiting for a provincial health plan to take effect.

basic-visitors-to-canada-insurance.name: Basic Visitors to Canada Insurance
basic-visitors-to-canada-insurance.description: Lower-cost emergency medical coverage for visitors on a budget.

student-insurance.name: Student Insurance
student-insurance.description: Cover for international students without a provincial health plan, and for Canadian students studying away. Includes medical and hospital treatment, some dental and eye care, and tutoring after a hospital stay.
student-insurance.eligibility: International students studying in Canada, and Canadian students studying out of province or abroad.

trip-cancellation-trip-interruption-insu.name: Trip Cancellation & Trip Interruption Insurance
trip-cancellation-trip-interruption-insu.description: Covers costs if a trip is cancelled before departure or disrupted during travel.

24-7-emergency-medical-assistance.name: 24/7 Emergency Medical Assistance
24-7-emergency-medical-assistance.description: Round-the-clock emergency medical assistance and claims support on 1-800-663-0399.

desjardins.tagline: Newcomer banking, credit building, and free legal help.
desjardins.description: Desjardins is Canada's largest cooperative financial group. Its newcomer offer includes a chequing account with no monthly plan fee during an eligibility period, no-annual-fee credit cards to help build Canadian credit history, and a free legal assistance service. Its branch network is in Quebec and Ontario.
highlights: No monthly plan fee during the newcomer period
Credit cards to build Canadian credit history
Free legal assistance service for two years
desjardins.eligibility: The newcomer account offer is for people aged 25 and over who are permanent residents, or temporary residents with a work permit valid for more than 8 months, who have lived in Canada 3 years or less and are not already Desjardins members. Separate offers cover ages 18–24 and full-time students aged 25–30.
desjardins.howToStart: Open an account online in about 15 minutes, or apply from abroad and confirm your identity at a service location on arrival.
desjardins.hours: Legal assistance: file opening 24/7 · advisors Mon–Fri 9:00am–8:00pm, Sat 9:00am–5:00pm

newcomers-chequing-account-unlimited-pla.name: Newcomers chequing account (Unlimited plan)
newcomers-chequing-account-unlimited-pla.description: Chequing account with the monthly Unlimited plan fee waived during the eligibility period.
newcomers-chequing-account-unlimited-pla.eligibility: Aged 25+, permanent resident or temporary resident with a work permit valid more than 8 months, in Canada 3 years or less, and not already a Desjardins member.

free-legal-assistance-service.name: Free legal assistance service
free-legal-assistance-service.description: Legal assistance included with the newcomer offer for two years, covering everyday matters.

international-money-transfers.name: International money transfers
international-money-transfers.description: International money transfers of up to $25,000 per day.

youth-and-student-accounts.name: Youth and student accounts
youth-and-student-accounts.description: Account offers for younger newcomers and full-time students.
youth-and-student-accounts.eligibility: Ages 18–24, or 25–30 if a full-time student.

howWeChoose.title: How we choose these
howWeChoose.intro: Unify lists organizations that help newcomers settle in British Columbia. Here is what we check before one goes on the list.

criteria.serves: They serve newcomers directly, and we name the area they cover.
criteria.published: Their services, hours, and contact details are published by the organization itself.
criteria.eligibility: We record who qualifies. Many settlement programs are open only to permanent residents and protected persons, so we say that up front.
criteria.reviewed: We check the list again over time and remove organizations that close or stop serving newcomers.

howWeChoose.footnote: This directory is a starting point, not legal or financial advice. Confirm the details with the organization before you visit. To report a missing or out-of-date listing, email contact@unifysocial.ca.
